multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which is the FIRST step of a sound troubleshooting methodology?

choice.div: Identify the problem and gather information.
Replace the most expensive suspect component.

div.p: Identify the problem first: what changed, when it started, who is affected, and whether it reproduces. Everything else follows from good information.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A browser cannot load a page. Applying "divide and conquer", which test best narrows the fault fastest?

choice.div: Ping a hostname and its IP to separate DNS from connectivity.

div.p: Testing name versus address separates the layers. It eliminates half the possible causes before you change anything.

choiceresponse.p: When should a ticket be escalated? Select all that apply.

choice.div: The problem is beyond your access or scope.
It may be a security incident.
You have spent your agreed window without progress.
Before asking the user any questions.

div.p: Escalate for access, scope, security risk, or time — with good notes. Escalation is a routing decision, not a failure.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A support technician wants to install a new tool. The best practice is to:

choice.div: Download it from any site that offers a free version.
Install from the organisation's approved source and check the licence.
Ask the user to install it themselves with admin rights.

div.p: Untrusted installers are a leading malware vector, and licence type matters. Use the approved, centrally managed deployment path.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: After passing this course, the recommended next course in the IT Support Specialist track is:

choice.div: A second attempt at this same course.

div.p: The track continues with deeper networking and systems administration, then security operations, then a capstone. Foundations is the first rung, not the last.
